title: KIEL-SKIN – Kiel Inflammatory Skin Disease Cohort
summary:
Chronic inflammatory skin diseases such as psoriasis, atopic dermatitis (eczema), and hidradenitis suppurativa can affect patients for many years. The aim of the KIEL-SKIN study is to better understand how these diseases are treated in routine clinical practice, how they develop over time, and which factors influence disease progression and treatment outcomes.

Patients of all ages who receive treatment for a chronic inflammatory skin disease at the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH), Campus Kiel, Germany, and provide written informed consent to participate in the study are eligible for inclusion.

The study uses only information collected as part of routine medical care. Following written informed consent, both existing data from previous treatments and information documented during future clinical visits may be used for scientific analysis. These data may include information on the disease, previous and current treatments, examination results, and quality of life, provided that such information has been recorded during routine clinical care.

No additional examinations, blood tests, medical appointments, or questionnaires are required for the study. Participation does not affect the medical treatment patients receive.

Data are pseudonymized for scientific analysis. This means that names and other directly identifying information are replaced with a code number. The study findings are intended to contribute to a better understanding and long-term improvement of care for people with chronic inflammatory skin diseases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinically documented chronic inflammatory skin disease, particularly psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, hidradenitis suppurativa, or another chronic inflammatory dermatosis; treatment at the Center for Inflammatory Skin Diseases, University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH), Campus Kiel; written study-specific informed consent. For minors, the required consent of the legal guardians and age-appropriate involvement of the child or adolescent are necessary. For non-German-speaking patients, comprehensible study information and informed consent must be ensured through qualified translation.
Exclusion criteria:
Absence of valid written study-specific informed consent; lack of capacity to provide informed consent in adults; for minors, absence of the required consent from legal guardians or objection by the child or adolescent; for non-German-speaking patients, inability to ensure comprehensible study information and informed consent through qualified translation.
